test_title: PYST 27: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the main feature of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025?

options.text: Implementation of Uniform Civil Code Guidelines
Inclusion of Muslim women and all sects on boards
Nationalisation of all registered Waqf properties
Abolition of all existing Waqf Boards

solution:
The correct answer is __**Inclusion of Muslim women and all sects on boards**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025** introduces measures to enhance inclusivity and diversity within Waqf Boards.
 
• One of the primary features of the amendment is the **inclusion of Muslim women** and members from all sects in the composition of Waqf Boards.
 
• This amendment aims to provide equal representation and participation of all sections of the Muslim community, ensuring gender equality and inclusiveness in decision-making processes.
 
• By including women and members of diverse sects, the Act addresses historical underrepresentation and ensures that the voices of all community members are heard.
 
• Such inclusiveness fosters a sense of unity and ensures transparency and accountability in the administration of Waqf properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Waqf:**

 
 
• The term **"Waqf"** refers to a religious endowment in Islam, typically involving property or assets dedicated to religious or charitable purposes.
 
• Waqf properties are managed by **Waqf Boards**, which are statutory bodies established under the Waqf Act.
 
• The primary purpose of Waqf properties is to serve the socio-economic and religious needs of the Muslim community.
 
 
 
• **Waqf Boards:**
 
 
• Waqf Boards are responsible for managing and overseeing Waqf properties, ensuring they are used for the benefit of the community.
 
• They function under the provisions of the **Waqf Act, 1995**, which was amended in **2013** and now again in 2025.
 
• The boards consist of members from various sections of the Muslim community, including religious scholars and government-nominated members.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Amendments in the Waqf Act:**
 
 
• The previous amendment in **2013** brought in significant changes, such as the establishment of a **Waqf Tribunal** for the resolution of disputes related to Waqf properties.
 
• The **2025 Amendment** further strengthens the representation of marginalized groups within the Waqf Boards.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Civil Code Guidelines:**
 
 
• The **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)** refers to a proposal to replace personal laws of various communities with a common set of laws applicable to all citizens of India.
 
• It has no direct connection with the **Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025**, making Option 1 incorrect.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nationalisation of all Waqf Properties:**

 
 
• Option 3 is incorrect, as the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, does not entail the **nationalization of Waqf properties**. Waqf properties continue to be managed by the respective Waqf Boards.
 
 
 
• **Abolition of Waqf Boards:**
 
 
• Option 4 is also incorrect. The amendment does not abolish the Waqf Boards but instead aims to make them more inclusive and representative of the Muslim community.
